scope: Evidence, workbook, table/editing, preferences, external integrations and release requirements

requirements.title: Versioned reference corpus and evidence provenance
acceptance: Retain source hash, version/platform, section/image identity and evidence type for every claim.
Separate Prism 10 author observations, documentation/resource-only statements, saved Prism 11 outputs, direct Prism 11 runtime tests and GP design choices.

requirements.title: Full guide and resource inventory traceability
acceptance: All 226 guide sections, 32 existing coverage families, 152 equation records and 82 in-table functions map to explicit requirements or source-context entries.
Every discovered menu/control/option/test example is triaged; new discoveries reopen affected requirements.

requirements.title: Executable macOS reference test harness
acceptance: Acquire authorized macOS execution and a usable Prism installation; retain app version, settings, inputs, outputs, screenshots and action traces.
Use copies of generated/supplied fixtures, not unrelated personal projects.
Do not certify unresolved runtime-only semantics from screenshots or decompilation.

requirements.title: Numerical comparison and rendering harness
acceptance: Compare structured output including missing/undefined states and numerical tolerances justified per quantity.
Compare screen and export geometry/fonts/ticks/colors/cropping against reference captures; review platform font differences explicitly.
Keep fixtures, provenance and test commands reproducible.

requirements.title: Resolve conflicting guide statements and versions
acceptance: Track conflicts without guessing: Column preaveraged conversion, Mac linked text import, script log encodings, recalculation on open, SVG scripting support.
Resolve each with versioned runtime or authoritative artifact evidence before parity closure.

requirements.title: Regression/CI release gates and persistent work queue
acceptance: Run schema, numeric, format, worker/server, interaction, browser and export checks appropriate to every changed subsystem.
A checked requirement has implementation plus GP tests; verified-equivalent additionally has adequate Prism references.
Keep each unmet requirement open with next action and blocker.
limitations: Workflow added and local commands validated; hosted Actions run not verified from this environment. Full per-requirement fixture coverage remains open.

requirements.title: Stable identities and versioned schema migrations
acceptance: Assign stable identities to rows, datasets, replicates, subjects, cells, analyses, graph objects and layout placements.
Migrate existing GP v1/v2 without losing drafts, links, settings, exclusions or results; reject malformed/cyclic/dangling references.
Rename/reorder/delete never silently retarget dependencies.
implementation_evidence: web/src/workbook.ts: GP workbook version 4 stores exclusions by stable dataset/row IDs; v2/v3 migrate and reject unsupported exclusion fields
limitations: Implemented stable identities cover current Column/XY sheets, datasets and represented rows; cells use dataset/row composites. Replicate/subject, rich graph-object and layout-placement families remain open.
Version3 is an independent GP schema. Native dataset GUID references support identity separation; native row-ID serialization and full file equivalence are not claimed.
Storage key gp.workbook.v2 is retained for compatibility; serialized document version is 4 (version 3 introduced identities; version 4 adds exclusions). Existing source files remain unmodified.
Version 4 is required for exclusions so older GP builds reject such files instead of silently re-including excluded values.
validation_evidence: web/src/workbook.test.ts: v1 draft/v2 saved-result migration; strict v3 dataset/row IDs and reference validation; duplicate names, reorder/insert/delete and explicit row mapping
web/src/workbook-actions.test.ts: fresh data-copy IDs and source-preserving graph copies
web/src/workbook-selection.test.ts: stable graph selection and source-cell navigation after source mutations

web/src/workbook-exclusions.test.ts: 10 tests covering toggle/mixed/restore, blank/draft/virtual cells, row insert/reorder/delete and dataset insert/delete identity tracking, edit/clear dropping only that exclusion, XY excluded X, undo/redo, frozen data/result/graph boundaries including revision reuse, v4 round trip, v3 migration and malformed-exclusion rejection, data-copy remapping and imported positions.

requirements.title: Automatic recomputation of existing direct analyses
acceptance: Editing or pasting valid data refreshes every eligible linked analysis without clicking Run.
Debounce incomplete typing, cancel superseded jobs and reject late responses after edits, undo, open/recovery and disposal.
Navigation and unrelated edits do not steal focus or suppress needed work.
Failures attach to the affected result, do not display old output as current or retry indefinitely.
Derived refreshes preserve undo/redo; static worker and server modes have matching behavior.
limitations: Only existing direct analyses of Column/XY data; dependency chains and freezing remain W003/W004.
Abort discards obsolete replies but does not physically interrupt Python already running in the static worker.
No live native Prism workflow comparison; this is GP behavior verified, not verified_equivalent.
validation_evidence: scripts/check_recalculation.py:actual calculation checks against server and static browser

requirements.title: General dependency graph and chained results
acceptance: Topologically update transforms, analyses of analyses, linked cells, info constants, graphs and layouts.
Detect cycles, fan-out, deletion, missing inputs and error propagation; unrelated families remain unchanged.
limitations: Current runtime consumers are direct data/results/graphs. Generic DAG support is not implementation of chained analyses, transforms, formula cells, Info constants, links or layouts.
Future chained execution must await completed upstream tasks, not merely use topological dispatch order. Those consumers remain tracked individually.
validation_evidence: web/src/workbook-dependencies.test.ts:16 tests including missing/wrong-kind inputs, source mismatch, SCC cycles, downstream isolation, frozen update barriers,30k chain and130k fan-out

18 recalculation regressions passed after schema migration, including freezing an undo-restored result while an obsolete request is running; scheduler consumes dependency ordering and isolates blocked families.

requirements.title: Freeze/unfreeze data, results and graphs
acceptance: Frozen data reject edits; frozen results and graphs retain their scientific snapshot when upstream data change.
Unfreeze updates downstream state; persistence, duplication, undo and export honor freeze state.
Determine native handling of changed parameters and frozen dependencies before parity closure.
prism_reference_evidence: docs/prism-freeze-rea-evidence.md: six bounded REA native handlers/callback with source ranges and hashes; shipped menu/toolbar and localized guidance retained separately
limitations: Current Column/XY families only; unsupported result exclusions, formulas/compatibility flags and native special unfreeze branches remain open.

Snapshot persistence, undo and direct recalculation on thaw are independently implemented GP behavior; underlying native setFrozen/storage/invalidation bodies and a running Prism comparison remain unresolved.

Frozen graph creation rejects stale or mismatched linked output. Historical result-to-new-live-graph and changed-source live export require explicit recalculation, avoiding silent recomputation of a captured curve.
Source-table deletion retains current family cascade, not full Prism orphan semantics. Large snapshots remain subject to workbook/browser-storage limits and recovery warnings.
Frozen data tables reject exclusion changes (GP choice). The shipped CoreLegacy string 1018 says frozen tables allow excluding values from results tables; results-side exclusion is not implemented.
validation_evidence: web/src/workbook-freeze.test.ts:15 cases covering snapshots, frozen output, guards, historical graph links, deletion, remapping, save/reopen, duplication and undo/redo

scripts/check_workbook_foundations.py:9 actual-browser scenario groups passed in development, packaged server and self-contained static builds. Static repeat completed245.93s with no page errors; original diagnostic failures retained outside Git.

requirements.title: Complete undo transactions and redo semantics
acceptance: Cover cell blocks, formats, exclusions, object edits, sheet/family operations, analysis parameters and scripts.
Continuous typing/dragging is grouped appropriately; Apply commits once; Cancel restores only uncommitted changes.
Async derived results neither add user edits nor erase redo; document replacements cancel outstanding work.
implementation_evidence: web/src/App.tsx: Exclude/Include values commit exactly one labelled history entry from menu, toolbar, cell context or graph point details
validation_evidence: web/src/workbook-exclusions.test.ts and scripts/check_exclusions.py: exclusion undo/redo restore the complete exclusion map and recalculated output.

requirements.title: Autosave, recovery, dirty state and multiple documents
acceptance: Separate saved-to-file, saved-in-browser and unsaved edits; recover crashes/quota failures without overwriting originals.
Implement new/open/recent/close/close-all/save/save-as/duplicate/revert/backup and independent open documents.
User-visible browser file limitations are concrete; do not claim native Finder document actions exist.

requirements.title: Complete five-section workbook navigation
acceptance: Data/Info/Results/Graphs/Layouts sections, searchable names, disclosure, New actions and current-family ordering.
Back/forward, previous-sheet switch, linked-sheet menu, sheet chooser, section shortcuts, show/hide navigator.
All actions retain identity and correct context under undo/delete/duplicate/import.

requirements.title: Gallery and thumbnail navigation
acceptance: Section/family galleries show live thumbnails and multi-selection; switch sheet/gallery without document mutation.
Large projects virtualize rendering and invalidate only affected thumbnails.

requirements.title: Sheet/family lifecycle and organization
acceptance: Create with/without graph; rename/reorder/multiselect/highlight/delete sheets.
Duplicate sheet and whole family with new identities and remapped internal links; save/export/print/delete family.
Deletion previews dependent consequences and supports undo; preserve shared sources correctly.

requirements.title: Info sheets and dynamic constants
acceptance: Named typed constants and free notes; default experiment metadata; add/remove/reorder/import rows.
Link/unlink table families; insert live info/analysis constants into text, axes, ticks and model constraints.
Rename/delete/invalid constants update dependents predictably and serialize losslessly.

requirements.title: Floating notes and scientific warning notes
acceptance: Create six colors; edit rich text/links; move/resize/minimize/delete; retain sheet association and undo.
Attach scientific diagnostics to results/graphs; manage focus and warning preferences without hiding failed fits.

requirements.title: Typed cell representation, missingness and exclusions
acceptance: Store value separately from missing/excluded/censored/error states; preserve raw entered text and precision.
Blank differs from zero; reversible exclusion retains original numeric value and affects analysis/graph/export consistently.
Support number, text, date and elapsed-time representations without unsafe coercion.
implementation_evidence: web/src/workbook.ts: DataSheet.excluded keyed by dataset ID → row IDs; canonicalExclusions, includedProject/selectedProject analysis view, toggleExcludedValues, sameSourceData, v4 validation/migration
web/src/DataGrid.tsx and web/src/data-grid.ts: blue italic asterisk cells, excluded ARIA label, Exclude/Include Values context command and shared allExcluded state
web/src/App.tsx: Edit menu, Data toolbar and graph point-details Exclude Values commands routed to one undoable command; status counts; results note; CSV export choice dialog
web/src/workbook-freeze.ts and web/src/workbook-actions.ts: frozen snapshots capture exclusions; data copies remap them to fresh identities
limitations: Implemented: reversible exclusion state separate from entered text, blank≠zero preserved, numeric-only exclusions, consistent omission from analyses, recalculation, plotted points and graph export.
Still open: typed text/date/elapsed-time representations, censored and error cell states, subject/replicate identities, and results-side exclusions.
GP choice: editing or clearing an excluded cell's text drops that exclusion (a new value is a new observation); row moves keep it. Native behavior for edited excluded cells is unverified.

No running Prism reference: blue-italic-asterisk display and calculation omission follow the public Prism guide (audit P0120); colors, spacing and toggle rule are GP choices, not compared screenshots or native traces.

Static self-contained build not exercised in the 2026-10-19 cloud container: its network policy denied cdn.jsdelivr.net, so scripts/build_browser.py could not fetch the locked Pyodide wheels. CI runs scripts/check_exclusions.py against both static and server builds; that hosted result has not been observed.
validation_evidence: web/src/workbook-exclusions.test.ts: 10 tests covering toggle/mixed/restore, blank/draft/virtual cells, row insert/reorder/delete and dataset insert/delete identity tracking, edit/clear dropping only that exclusion, XY excluded X, undo/redo, frozen data/result/graph boundaries including revision reuse, v4 round trip, v3 migration and malformed-exclusion rejection, data-copy remapping and imported positions.

scripts/check_exclusions.py on the packaged server build (2026-10-19, Chromium 1194): 10 scenario groups passed with zero page errors — context menu, toolbar and Edit menu toggles; computed blue italic style and asterisk; actual recalculated means and analysis payload nulls; results note; drawn graph points and graph-export payload; graph point Exclude Values with undo; reload persistence; CSV asterisk export and re-import; Prism XML Excluded import; frozen-table command disabling.
web/src/workbook.test.ts and existing suites: 157 frontend tests and TypeScript passed after the v4 schema change; 268 backend tests passed.

requirements.title: Raw Column table: stacked and paired entry
acceptance: Independent unequal-length columns and matched rows with subject IDs; pairing set explicitly in analysis.
Missing pairs and missing repeated measures follow verified analysis rules.

requirements.title: XY table: X formats and replicate Y layouts
acceptance: Numeric X, horizontal X errors, dates and elapsed time; reference origin/units and locale parsing.
Single Y, replicate subcolumns, raw plotting and correct numeric spacing; row titles are not X data.
Zero concentration controls are supported where model mathematics permits; log-concentration remains a different input domain.

requirements.title: Preaveraged and asymmetric error entry
acceptance: Mean/SD/SE/CV with or without N; plus/minus errors; low/high and explicit upper/lower limits.
Relabeling SD/SEM does not numerically convert observations; table conversion behavior is explicit and tested.
Only mathematically supported analyses run; raw-only residual/repeated-measures options are unavailable.

requirements.title: Native Grouped tables and subject matching
acceptance: Row/column factors, replicate subcolumns, mean/error entry, missing cells and factor labels.
Support subject-along-rows and subject-across-columns matching; preserve experimental unit identity.
Represent documented three-way 2×2×K encoding and integrate existing standalone ANOVA workspace.

requirements.title: Contingency tables
acceptance: Integer nonnegative counts, row/outcome labels, zero-margin validation; reject percentage/continuous inputs.
Use correct orientation for prospective/retrospective and diagnostic analyses.

requirements.title: Native Survival tables
acceptance: Time plus sparse per-group event/censor indicators, subject IDs, elapsed time or start/end dates.
Create survival analysis and graph automatically; integrate existing KM/logrank workspace.
Validate ties, censoring, missing membership, nonpositive/invalid times according to references.

requirements.title: Parts-of-whole tables
acceptance: Category titles, values/counts, expected distributions; correct zero-total and invalid-negative behavior.
Feed fraction, goodness-of-fit and pie/donut/stacked plots.

requirements.title: Multiple-variable tables
acceptance: Label/continuous/categorical/text variables, reference levels, subject rows and numeric precision.
Explicit type conversion, missing policy, group-variable mapping and graph axis-variable assignment.

requirements.title: Nested tables
acceptance: Treatment datasets contain experimental-unit subcolumns containing technical observations with unequal n.
Experimental units drive degrees of freedom; no silent flattening of technical replicates.

requirements.title: Format Data Table and loss-aware conversions
acceptance: Change kind, subcolumns, errors, date origins/units with a review of data that no longer fit.
Undo restores full original; compatible analyses/graphs remap and recalculate; incompatible dependents are explicit.

requirements.title: Row and dataset titles and per-cell display formatting
acceptance: Independent labels, hide/show row titles, fixed dataset lettering, replicate headers, decimal display and cell highlights.
Labels propagate to results/legends/category axes without changing numeric precision.
Selected-point formatting links to the corresponding graph observations by identity.

requirements.title: Spreadsheet selection and keyboard navigation
acceptance: Single cell, rectangular/disjoint ranges, row/column/all selection, anchor/extent and scrolling.
Arrow/Tab/Enter/Shift movement, edit mode, selection shortcuts, delete/clear and clipboard act on correct cells.
Test focus, accessibility, bounds, virtualized large tables and browser-reserved shortcut alternatives.

requirements.title: Insert/delete/reorder/sort data blocks
acceptance: Insert cells/rows/datasets/subcolumns, clear versus delete, sort X/row-title and reverse row order.
Move all related replicate/error/subject metadata together; stable links/exclusions survive; undo is atomic.

requirements.title: Create numeric series
acceptance: Linear/geometric/time sequences with start/end/step/count; overflow/domain/cell-placement validation.
Preview resulting block and apply as one undoable edit.

requirements.title: Clipboard copy/cut/paste/transpose and Paste Special
acceptance: Parse numeric and HTML/text clipboard precision, titles, subcolumns, locale/decimal separators and missing/excluded modes.
Paste placement/filtering/transposition, multi-cell cut/undo and incomplete clipboard payloads are tested.
Browser permission errors provide supported file/manual alternatives without data loss.

requirements.title: Live linked data/result blocks
acceptance: Paste Link records typed range references, read-only red-outline destination and native update semantics.
Unlink/Format/Update and double-click editing preserve values; cycles and missing sources are detected.

requirements.title: Text file import and project merge
acceptance: CSV/TXT/DAT/PRN delimiters/encoding/headers/filters/placement, all supported table forms and preview.
Merge projects remaps identities and preserves dependencies; distinguish open/import/merge.
Mac direct Excel import is not assumed; test supported HTML clipboard instead.
implementation_evidence: web/src/data.ts importCsvWithExclusions and App CSV import: numbers followed by an asterisk import as excluded values, with a notice
limitations: Asterisk recognition is automatic on GP CSV import, not the Prism import/Paste Special filter option.

requirements.title: Exclusion UI and output policy
acceptance: Toggle excluded selected cells without deleting values; blue italic/asterisk display and status explanations.
Exclude from calculations and plotted observations; clipboard/export choices number/asterisk/blank preserve intended semantics.
Undo/reload/native file roundtrip retain exclusions; results-side exclusion maps to source identities.
implementation_evidence: web/src/workbook.ts: DataSheet.excluded keyed by dataset ID → row IDs; canonicalExclusions, includedProject/selectedProject analysis view, toggleExcludedValues, sameSourceData, v4 validation/migration
web/src/DataGrid.tsx and web/src/data-grid.ts: blue italic asterisk cells, excluded ARIA label, Exclude/Include Values context command and shared allExcluded state
web/src/App.tsx: Edit menu, Data toolbar and graph point-details Exclude Values commands routed to one undoable command; status counts; results note; CSV export choice dialog

gp/import_prism.py: Prism XML Excluded=1/true and EVFormat=AsteriskAfterNumber cells import their original numbers with explicit [column,row] exclusions
web/src/data.ts: exportCsv excluded-value modes value/asterisk/blank; importCsvWithExclusions recognizes a number followed by an asterisk
limitations: Implemented: toggle selected values without deleting them; blue italic asterisk display with an ARIA/tooltip explanation; calculation, graph and export-input omission; undo, reload, JSON save/open and Prism XML import retain exclusions; CSV export/copy offer number/asterisk/blank when a table has exclusions.

Open: grid Copy selected cells/⌘C still copies entered text without an excluded-value policy or copy preference (P0166); no TXT/XML data export; ZIP import still rejects EXCLUDED cell flags because their row encoding is not documented in committed evidence; no native XML export round trip; results-side exclusions and exclusion of fit points from results are absent; no keyboard shortcut because no native key equivalent was recovered.
Toggle rule (restore only when every numeric selected value is already excluded) is a GP choice; Prism's excludeValues: handler is untraced.

No running Prism reference: blue-italic-asterisk display and calculation omission follow the public Prism guide (audit P0120); colors, spacing and toggle rule are GP choices, not compared screenshots or native traces.

requirements.title: Welcome/project creation, tutorials and portfolio
acceptance: Eight table-family previews/options; create empty or tutorial; open/recent/clone tabs; template/example/method entry points.
Every supported tutorial opens with correct data layout, links and explanatory notes; catalogue tracks missing examples explicitly.
Do not redistribute proprietary assets as GP interface assets.

requirements.title: Context menus, compact toolbars and command routing
acceptance: Map every documented menu/toolbar command to a real capability and precise disabled reason until implemented.
Sheet-specific groups and two-row toolbar; menus/shortcuts/context commands share handlers and enabled state.
Record all Prism 11 resource commands missing from the guide as further requirements.

requirements.title: Status bar, zoom, inspector, rulers and viewport
acceptance: Show/hide toolbar/navigator/inspector/status, sheet/gallery/section controls and contextual cell or graph coordinates.
Zoom-to-page/graph, 50–1000%, reset preferences, graph/layout rulers/grid and accessibility remain coherent.

requirements.title: Appearance, typography, accessibility and native interaction fidelity
acceptance: Light/dark/system, correct white sheet/graph surfaces, font metrics, tab/field spacing, keyboard focus and dialog placement.
Screen reader semantics, high DPI, focus return, Escape, modal nesting, keyboard alternatives and resize/mobile fallback.
Compare reference screenshots and interactions for every implemented screen; do not equate theme with pixel parity.

requirements.title: View preferences
acceptance: Persist table/navigator/note fonts, inches/cm, zoom/reset, combined Data+Results folder, tooltips/warnings and alert reset.
Spell checking/autocomplete titles, locale date order and axis minus-glyph setting; preferences affect correct scope only.

requirements.title: New graph defaults and style scope
acceptance: Persist shape/dimensions/frame/thickness/ticks/fonts/symbols/lines/bar/error/spacing/jitter/color/decimal/title/page/text/table defaults.
New graphs inherit defaults; existing graphs only change through explicit Magic/style application.

requirements.title: Analysis defaults and result number formats
acceptance: P-value scientific/decimal thresholds, row/title truncation, per-analysis saved-default option groups and reset.
Default choice never rewrites existing analysis specification.

requirements.title: File/clipboard/print/location/Info defaults
acceptance: Autosave interval/on-navigation; clipboard blanks/exclusions/precision/separators/background; native compatibility setting.
Print grid/labels/header metadata, browser-accessible remembered locations, default Info constants and auto-creation.

requirements.title: Diagnostics, help and update information
acceptance: Help, contextual guides, tutorial pointers, appropriate-test checklists and reproducible error logs.
Report GP version/build and update availability honestly; do not present a GraphPad license or claim access to its private account services.

requirements.title: Cloud/power/QuickCalcs/GraphPad account services
acceptance: Catalogue every external service interaction and identify supported public links versus authenticated APIs.
Actual account-based integration requires documented API/access and user-authorized credentials; never implement fake successful login/publication/license checks.
Keep unavailable third-party functionality open as external dependency; browser substitute is not silently counted as native equivalence.

requirements.title: LabArchives and native office/share integrations
acceptance: Specify LabArchives, PowerPoint, Keynote, Word, mail/share-sheet behaviors and test supported API/file/clipboard adapters.
Record platform/browser limitations and actual access prerequisites; no unrequested external messages or publication.

requirements.title: Large-project performance and resource limits
acceptance: Benchmark large matrices, many sheets/objects, worker memory, fit cancellation and rendering responsiveness.
Bound parsing/execution/output allocations; limits are visible and tested, not silent truncation.
Virtualize tables/navigators and cache only by complete versioned inputs.

requirements.title: Malformed files, data isolation and fault recovery
acceptance: Validate archive expansion/path traversal/duplicate IDs/cyclic references/nonfinite values/corrupt binaries.
Treat imported scripts as data until user runs them; restrict script file access to selected workspaces/files.
Recover quota, worker failure, interrupted import/save and network failure without losing source files.

requirements.title: Supported browser/OS and accessible workflow matrix
acceptance: Test Chromium, Firefox and Safari/WebKit desktop; macOS keyboard behavior and high-DPI; mobile fallback.
Test cold/offline-capable static runtime, server mode, downloads, file picker/clipboard capabilities and preference storage failures.

requirements.title: Public deployment identity and production verification
acceptance: Embed immutable source/build identity and deployment metadata in served app.
Verify gp.samgillman.org HTML/assets/version against expected Git commit and production smoke workflows; stale cache/service worker cannot hide updates.
Verify Cloudflare build settings, preview/production separation, rollback and failed-build reporting.
If network or hosting access is unavailable, record exact blocker and never claim live deployment verified.

requirements.title: Reference-driven end-to-end acceptance and release audit
acceptance: Execute every guide recipe end-to-end across all table families and compare applicable Prism 11 numerical/format/UI/export outputs.
Reconcile every requirement, model, function, command, source section and unresolved native finding with implementation and evidence.
No open material requirement or unknown reference behavior can be silently waived or replaced by a percentage.
Publish exact supported limitations and obtain an explicit scope decision for unavoidable native/service dependencies before claiming full completion.
